description: RESIDUAL AUTOMATON LEAK via default tags. For a non-Automaton article, the only loud guard protects NOTE_NUM (lines 12-13). NOTE_TAGS has no guard: if a publisher sets NOTE_NUM (so the NUM guard passes) but forgets NOTE_TAGS, line 16 silently falls back to the Automaton tag set 'AI,AIエージェント,暗号資産,Automaton,自律AI' and line 49 publishes those tags onto the non-Automaton article. Spec INV-2 explicitly enumerates 'JP tags' as an Automaton value that must NOT leak. The builder added a loud refusal for NUM precisely because a silent Automaton default is dangerous, but left the equally-dangerous Automaton-tag default unguarded — so a real Automaton value (the tags) can reach update_article for a non-Automaton article. This is a genuine residual leak path, not merely an env default, because the rest of the article is non-Automaton while the tags are Automaton.
fix: Apply the same _is_automaton guard to tags (and ideally IMG_DIR/INFOG/SRC defaults): when NOT _is_automaton and NOTE_TAGS is unset, refuse loudly (SystemExit) instead of defaulting to the Automaton tag list. Equivalently, only fall back to the Automaton tag string when _is_automaton is true; otherwise require NOTE_TAGS explicitly. The test must then assert that a non-Automaton run with NOTE_TAGS UNSET either refuses or produces non-Automaton tags.
